title: HR Administrator
description:
Keeping people processes running smoothly makes a real difference to every employee, from their first day to their last. As an HR Administrator, you'll help make that happen, ensuring employees receive the right support, information and documentation at every stage of their employment.
You'll be joining a global manufacturing business in Milton Keynes that holds Investors in People Gold accreditation, reflecting its commitment to supporting and developing its workforce. This 12-month maternity cover contract offers the opportunity to get involved in a wide range of people processes, working closely with the management team in an established organisation.
What's in it for you
- Salary of up to 35,000 per annum.
- A 12-month fixed-term contract with a global manufacturing business.
- Flexibility within a full-time position.
- The opportunity to work for an Investors in People Gold accredited employer.
- Exposure to the full employee lifecycle, from recruitment and onboarding to payroll and employee development.
- Involvement in projects, process improvements and initiatives that support the wider workforce.

Your responsibilities as an HR Administrator
- Coordinate recruitment administration, onboarding, right-to-work checks, contractual changes and leaver processes.
- Prepare contracts, offer letters and employment documentation, ensuring records remain accurate and GDPR compliant.
- Support payroll by collating and submitting employee information, including starters, leavers and contractual changes.
- Maintain absence, annual leave and training records, including coordinating learning and development activities.
- Produce reports, maintain employee data and support audits, policy updates and process improvements.
- Work closely with employees, managers and external providers to ensure people processes run efficiently.

What we're looking for in an HR Administrator
- Previous experience in an HR administration or assistant role, with knowledge of employee lifecycle processes.
- A good understanding of UK employment legislation, GDPR and confidential employee data handling.
- Experience preparing employment documentation, maintaining records and supporting payroll administration.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Word and Outlook, with experience using HR systems.
- A CIPD Level 3 or Level 5 qualification would be advantageous but is not essential.

Working hours: Full-time, with flexibility available. Specific working hours to be confirmed.
If you're looking for an HR Administrator position where you can put your experience to good use, support employees across the business and contribute to an established people function, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today!

title: HR Administrator
description:
HR Administrator

Central Milton Keynes Hybrid Working Salary: Up to 30,000 + Benefits

Are you an organised and detail-focused HR professional looking for your next challenge within a fast-paced, growing business?

We are recruiting on behalf of a successful and expanding organisation for an HR Administrator to join a busy HR team based in Milton Keynes. This is an excellent opportunity for someone with previous HR experience who thrives in a high-volume environment and enjoys providing outstanding support to employees and stakeholders across the business.

The Role

As HR Administrator, you will play a key role in supporting the entire employee life-cycle, taking ownership of onboarding and off boarding processes while acting as a first point of contact for HR-related queries.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Managing the onboarding process from offer stage through to successful completion of probation
- Preparing and issuing offer letters, contracts and employment documentation
- Coordinating new starter administration and ensuring a smooth employee experience
- Managing the leaver process, including exit interviews and HR system updates
- Maintaining accurate employee records and ensuring HR data is consistently up to date
- Managing a central HR inbox and responding to employee and manager enquiries
- Supporting with queries relating to benefits, payroll, holiday entitlement, maternity, paternity and general HR policies
- Liaising with stakeholders across the business to provide timely and accurate HR support
- Assisting with visa and right-to-work checks where required

About You

We're looking for an energetic and highly organised HR professional who is able to manage multiple priorities while maintaining exceptional accuracy.

You'll ideally have:
- Around 2+ years' experience within an HR Administration or HR Assistant role
- Strong understanding of employee life-cycle processes
- Excellent administration and organisational skills
- Outstanding attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy
- Confidence managing high volumes of work and competing priorities
- Strong written and verbal communication skills
- The ability to work independently while building positive relationships with stakeholders

CIPD Level 3 qualification would be advantageous but is not essential.

Experience with visa administration or right-to-work checks would also be beneficial, although full training can be provided.

What's Important

This is a busy HR environment where attention to detail is absolutely critical. The successful candidate must be able to manage a high volume of administration, ensure nothing is overlooked, and maintain accurate employee records at all times.

The business operates internationally across multiple time zones, so flexibility is important. Standard hours are 9:00am to 5:00pm; however, occasional early starts or later finishes may be required to support global stakeholders.

Benefits
- Salary up to 30,000
- 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays
- Private healthcare
- Pension scheme
- Hybrid working
- Staff parking

If you're a motivated HR professional who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment and can demonstrate exceptional attention to detail, we'd love to hear from you.

Please be aware this advert will remain open until the vacancy has been filled. Interviews will take place throughout this period, therefore we encourage you to apply early to avoid disappointment.

Tate is committed to promoting equal opportunities. Your comfort and accessibility are our priority, and we are here to support you every step of the way. title: Hr Administrator
description:
Our client is an established international organisation operating across the UK and Europe, delivering complex projects for clients in a range of specialist and operational sectors.

The business works closely with its customers and supply chain partners to deliver projects efficiently, with a strong focus on safety, quality and positive outcomes.

The Role

The HR Administrator plays a key role in delivering an efficient, compliant and high-quality HR service across the full employee lifecycle.

The role is responsible for the day-to-day coordination and administration of HR processes, ensuring accuracy, strong audit trails and compliance with UK employment law, right to work requirements and relevant industry standards.

Main Duties and Responsibilities

Administration
- Act as the first point of contact for UK HR queries, providing a responsive and professional service.
- Maintain accurate employee data within HR systems promptly and correctly.
- Support management of the HR inbox, responding within agreed timeframes and ensuring documentation is complete, compliant and stored in line with GDPR and audit requirements.

Onboarding and New Starters
- Own the onboarding process from pre-employment through to the first week, including managing communications, coordinating and hosting inductions, and ensuring all compliance requirements are met.
- Ensure new starters are accurately set up across HR systems, payroll and benefits, with complete and compliant employee records maintained.

Payroll and Benefits
- Own the preparation and accuracy of monthly payroll data, including starters, leavers, contractual changes and other updates.
- Maintain payroll trackers and audit trails, resolve payroll queries and support the smooth running of the monthly payroll cycle.
- Manage employee benefits, liaise with providers where needed, and process HR-related invoices accurately and on time.

Global Mobility and Compliance
- Own the administration and tracking of relevant international work documentation and visa requirements, ensuring records are accurate and up to date.
- Maintain right to work documentation and support with sponsor licence requirements, escalating any risks or upcoming deadlines as needed.

Time, Attendance and Leave
- With support from the HR Advisor, administer annual leave, sickness absence and family-friendly leave processes, ensuring all data is accurately recorded within HR systems.
- Support managers with basic absence queries and ensure relevant information is captured and shared with the HR Advisor in a timely manner.

Employee Relations Support
- Provide administrative support across employee relations processes, including preparing letters, meeting notes and documentation.
- Support the HR Advisor and HR Manager with case administration, ensuring records are accurate, well organised and maintained in line with confidentiality and compliance requirements.

Reporting and HR Data
- Maintain accurate people data and support the production of regular HR reports, including joiners, leavers, absence and payroll inputs.
- Ensure trackers and reporting data are consistently updated, reliable and available to support business decision-making.

Continuous Improvement
- Contribute suggestions and recommendations for process improvement and participate in wider HR projects.
- Identify opportunities to improve HR processes and administrative efficiency, supporting ongoing system and process improvements.
- Contribute to standardising HR practices and support wider HR projects as required.

Skills and Experience
- Strong communication skills and excellent attention to detail.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office and HRIS systems.
- Ability to learn quickly and work effectively under pressure.
- Good time-management and prioritisation skills.
- Experience in HR administration or a similar role, ideally within a project-based, operational or construction-related environment.

title: HR Assistant Manager
description:
We're recruiting a 12-month fixed-term maternity cover for an experienced HR Assistant Manager to support multiple office locations including Milton Keynes, Peterborough and Birmingham. This is a hands-on, operational People role combining employee relations, stakeholder coaching, people projects, and team leadership within a growing and ambitious business.

Client Details

Our client is a leading UK professional services organisation with a strong people-first culture and ambitious growth plans. Following significant investment and continued expansion, they are looking for an experienced HR professional to join their People team and provide support across several regional offices, partnering closely with managers and employees to deliver a high-quality HR service.

Description

As a People Manager, you will provide pragmatic and commercially focused HR support across a portfolio of office locations, working closely with leaders and employees to drive positive people outcomes.

Key responsibilities include:
- Managing a broad range of employee relations cases, including performance management, absence, disciplinary, grievance and capability matters.
- Providing generalist HR advice and guidance to managers and employees.
- Coaching and developing a junior member of the People team.
- Supporting organisational and people-related projects.
- Building strong relationships with stakeholders across multiple sites.
- Promoting best practice and ensuring HR policies and processes are applied consistently.
- Analysing trends and identifying opportunities to improve employee experience and people processes.
- Supporting business growth by partnering with operational leaders on workforce and people matters.
- This is a hybrid role requiring regular travel between offices in Milton Keynes, Peterborough and Leicester, with occasional travel to Birmingham as required. Travel expenses are fully covered in line with company policy.

Profile

The successful candidate will be an experienced HR professional who enjoys building relationships, solving problems and providing practical, people-focused advice.

You will ideally have:
- Previous experience in a generalist HR position such as HR Advisor, HR Business Partner or People Manager.
- Strong employee relations experience and confidence managing a range of ER cases independently.
- Experience coaching, mentoring or managing more junior team members.
- Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
- A professional, credible and approachable style with the ability to engage employees at all levels.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage a varied workload across multiple locations.
- A proactive and positive approach, with a genuine passion for HR and supporting people.
- A full UK driving licence and willingness to travel regularly between regional offices.

Job Offer

Competitive salary, negotiable depending on experience.

12-month fixed-term contract covering maternity leave.

Hybrid working model with flexibility around working hours.

37.5-hour working week with core hours of 10am-2pm.

Business travel expenses covered.

25 days annual leave plus bank holidays

Opportunity to join a growing organisation with strong investment and ambitious plans.

Supportive leadership team and collaborative People function.

Immediate impact role with genuine autonomy and stakeholder exposure.
